insight: For Jordan, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have had a notable impact on their gameplay momentum. When they weren't pressing before a break, they managed to gain momentum in most cases, with an average change of +0.040 minutes, suggesting that these breaks allowed them to regroup and come back stronger. However, when Jordan was pressing before a break, they lost momentum significantly, with an average change of -0.300 minutes, indicating that their intense pressure may have left them exhausted and vulnerable after the pause. Overall, the data suggests that Jordan tends to benefit from hydration breaks when they're not exerting excessive energy beforehand, allowing them to recharge and maintain their momentum in the game.
